title: NOAA low-probability flood weeks had 57 confirmed events against a risk bound sum of 29 in January to October 2026
abstract: We tested whether repeated flood days explain a daily probability deficit in the NOAA monthly flood outlook. We used a standard union bound to test any-flood risk in a week without a model of dependence between its days. Missing observations count as no confirmed flood, so they cannot create the count excess. Among 1,905 station-weeks at 66 gauges, all seven daily probabilities were below 5% in one issued run. Floods were confirmed in 57 weeks against a rounding-adjusted upper risk bound sum of 29.1235. The ratio was 1.96. The primary conditional 95% rate-gap interval from nominal 30-day calendar blocks was -0.059 to +3.415 percentage points; it included zero. A nominal 60-day interval excluded zero. All seven week start dates and all leave-one-month-out point gaps were positive. Removing the five calendar weeks with the largest gaps reduced the excess by 95%. Thus the earlier daily count deficit gives weaker evidence at the weekly episode scale. Three-day episodes retained a positive interval; fourteen-day episodes did not. The test adds an observation-gap-safe method and qualifies the strength of the daily evidence. It does not identify a physical cause or establish a stable weekly error. Limits include one incomplete year, selected gauges, stronger full-schedule calibration assumptions, and block uncertainty. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure, independent arithmetic checks and exact provenance for 142 shared source files are included. Raw and record-level external data stay outside the package.

display.caption: Confirmed occupied episodes and conservative upper risk bound sums. All daily probabilities are below 5% in one forecast run. Calendar block intervals allow shared events across gauges. The primary weekly nominal 30-day interval includes zero. Episode lengths select different samples.

citations.reason: Reuses frozen source snapshots, unchanged reconstruction and retrieval code. Adds an episode risk bound and observation-gap-safe counting; qualifies the strength of the earlier daily result.
